Note::is_text¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

bool Note::is_text() const noexcept

Distinguish Validated Text From Raw Bytes¶

is_text() reports whether the receiver stores validated UTF-8 text lanes. It is deliberately distinct from is_bytes: Bytes may contain arbitrary octets, including embedded zero bytes and invalid UTF-8, while Text participates in character-, grapheme-, case-, and language-aware operations.

The method checks the storage tag only. It does not rescan UTF-8, inspect every cell, or claim that a Bytes payload could not be decoded. Use to_utf8_strict() or to_utf8_lossy() when conversion is intended. Most text transformations preserve Text dtype, whereas predicates and measurements intentionally return Bool or Int64 Notes.

The query is constant-time, allocation-free, and noexcept. It is independent of rank and cell contents. Undefined returns false, so test defined() as well when absence must be reported separately.

Example 1: Text And Bytes Are Different Contracts¶

const auto text = pluss::note::make("alpha");
const auto bytes = pluss::note::bytes(std::string_view{"A\0B", 3});
const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "text=" << text.is_text()
          << " bytes=" << bytes.is_text()
          << " absent=" << absent.is_text() << '\n';

Output¶

text=true bytes=false absent=false

The embedded zero is retained by Bytes; it is not treated as a C-string terminator.

Example 2: A Text Transformation Preserves Dtype¶

const auto lowered = pluss::note::make("Alpha").lower();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "lowered=" << lowered.is_text()
          << " value=" << lowered.scalar() << '\n';

Output¶

lowered=true value=alpha

Example 3: A Predicate Changes The Result Dtype¶

const auto mask = pluss::note::make({"alpha", "beta"}).contains("a");
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "text=" << mask.is_text()
          << " bool=" << mask.is_bool() << '\n';

Output¶

text=false bool=true
